# Third-party notices

`actlith` ships **0 direct dependencies**, which pulls in 0 crates in
total. This file says what they are, why each direct one is there rather
than hand-rolled, and what licence the set carries.

## Why there are none yet

The project's own constraint is *keep dependencies minimal, and justify
each one in `SPEC.md` R*. The crate so far is a stub; `clap` (D15) joins
with the command line, and its row lands here with it.

## The full set

Every crate reachable from a normal (non-dev, non-build) dependency edge
of `actlith`:

| Crate | Version | Licence |
| --- | --- | --- |
<!-- END crates -->

Every crate is available under MIT, so the whole tree can be taken under
MIT alongside this project.

The table is a readable copy of what `Cargo.lock` resolves, rendered by
`actlith-dev notices` (dev/), and the `notices` step fails when the two
differ.

## Not dependencies: the tools in the gate

These appear in the dev shell and the gate, and are **not** linked into
`actlith`. A consumer building the crate never sees them.

- [`hk`](https://github.com/jdx/hk): the gate runner.
- [`pkl`](https://github.com/apple/pkl): evaluates `hk.pkl`.
- [`pklith`](https://github.com/pr0d1r2/pklith): materializes the hk
  steps from `.pklith`.
- [`microlith`](https://github.com/pr0d1r2/microlith) (`mth`): owns the
  `SPEC.md` format and checks it.
- [`sherd`](https://github.com/pr0d1r2/sherd): checks the federated spec
  and holds the coverage floor.
- [`itok`](https://github.com/pr0d1r2/itok): token counting for the
  per-file ceilings.
- [`actionlint`](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) and
  [`zizmor`](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor): lint the workflows.
